result.rationale: The rescue objective (0/2 civilians) never progresses across all 6 turns despite the team repeatedly reaching relevant zones. The dominant causal blocker is survival/spatial pressure: Engineer Imani is repeatedly damaged by Raider Holt's scatter-blast (100→71→46) and by the reactor environment hazard (46→36→26→16), dropping to 16/100 health by turn 6. Reactor heat climbs monotonically 62→70→78→86→94→100, crossing the threshold and dealing 10 damage per turn to anyone in reactor zones (Imani, Chen, Veyra). Meanwhile the medic escorting Sato is repeatedly contested on zone capacity (turn 4 medic-reyes contested target_zone_capacity_lost), and the team's split formation leaves Imani exposed in the reactor corridor while Chen is pinned at reactor-entry. The useful affordance (rescuing civilians) is locally legible and repeatedly attempted (recover-civilian responsibilities on kade and sato every turn), but hostile spatial pressure and health attrition block the actors before the rescue can complete. This is not an information bottleneck (map is fully revealed by turn 2) nor a local-policy-choice failure (the agent consistently pursues the correct objective). The bottleneck is survival/spatial pressure: health, reactor hazard, and zone capacity prevent the rescue from becoming actionable.
